tagline: Southern Africa's Atlantic giant — a Portuguese-inflected city of 8 million with an island promenade and a fortress above the bay.
overview: Luanda grew from a 1576 Portuguese port into southern Africa's largest city — an Atlantic capital of 8 million where colonial facades survive beside oil-money towers on the Marginal waterfront.

The city's spine is the Ilha — a sandy spit lined with restaurants and clubs that locals treat as the weekend — while the Fortaleza de São Miguel's 16th-century walls look down on the bay from above the old town. Kizomba, the sensual dance music born here, went global from these clubs.
Speed's 2025 Africa tour streamed from Luanda. Oil wealth made it famously expensive for expats, though street life — grilled fish at the Ilha, funana dancing — stays resolutely affordable.
